raw-meat-raw-liver-diet.summary: Eating uncooked meat, organs and dairy in the hope of more natural growth hormone and IGF-1, better skin and stronger development.

quick.overview:
The raw meat or raw liver diet means eating animal foods, including organs such as liver and heart, uncooked. Followers on looksmax.org are after fuller physical development, better skin and sturdier bones, which they link to higher natural IGF-1 and growth hormone.

The idea is that raw animal foods keep nutrients that cooking degrades, and that those nutrients support the body's own growth signalling. No human trials have tested the diet for appearance outcomes. Raw liver is a rich source of vitamins and minerals, including preformed vitamin A.
quick.how: Members describe plans built around raw milk products, raw organs such as liver and heart, raw meat and fish, and occasional fruit with few or no vegetables. It is usually followed as an all-in eating pattern over months rather than a single add-on, and some members say they follow it to support development during puberty. Other members call it TikTok hype.
quick.risks: Reviews and case reports link raw liver to tapeworm infection, fascioliasis, toxoplasmosis, toxocariasis and halzoun syndrome, and undercooked pork products to hepatitis E. Thorough cooking kills parasites, viruses and most bacteria. A single slice of beef liver can exceed the tolerable upper intake for preformed vitamin A. Pregnant people, children and anyone with a weakened immune system face the highest risk from foodborne infection.

angle.text: Followers eat raw meat, organs and dairy expecting more natural IGF-1 and growth hormone, which they link to better skin, stronger bones and fuller physical development. The expected gains come from proponents' theory and personal reports; the medical literature in this area mainly describes infections tied to raw liver and undercooked meat.

raw-milk.summary: Unpasteurized milk drunk in primal and carnivore circles for height, skin, digestion and hormones; reviews find small nutritional differences from pasteurized milk.

quick.overview:
Raw milk is milk that has not been heat-treated. In looksmaxxing and primal-diet circles it is drunk for a nutrient-dense, enzyme-rich food that supporters say helps skin, hormones, digestion and, in adolescents, height.

Proponents say heat destroys enzymes, immunoglobulins, vitamins and beneficial bacteria, so unheated milk keeps more of them active. A 2011 systematic review of 40 studies found pasteurization lowers some vitamins (B1, B2, C, folate) slightly and has a minimal effect on overall nutritive value. Some forum members note that milk cannot change bone length after growth plates fuse.
quick.how: People buy it from farms or shops where sale is allowed and drink it as a staple, often as part of carnivore or primal eating, with some discussing large intakes for body-composition goals. Reports of results come from personal experience over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Raw milk can carry Listeria, Salmonella, E. coli and Campylobacter, and pregnant women, children, older adults and immunocompromised people are at greatest risk of serious illness. Public-health literature also links it to brucellosis and tick-borne encephalitis. Legal status varies: some places ban retail sale, others allow farm sales with labels. Some forum members report acne or bloating.

angle.text: In primal and carnivore-style circles raw milk is drunk for height in adolescents, clearer skin, digestion and hormones, on the idea that unheated milk keeps more nutrients and enzymes active. A 2011 review found pasteurization changes nutritive value only minimally.

seed-oil-avoidance.summary: Cutting canola, soybean, sunflower and similar oils for clearer skin, less puffiness and general health, usually in favour of butter, tallow or olive oil.

quick.overview:
Seed oil avoidance means removing refined vegetable oils such as canola, soybean, sunflower, corn and safflower and cooking with fats like butter, tallow or olive oil. People do it for clearer skin, less puffiness and a leaner look, which they link to lower inflammation.

Proponents point to omega-6 linoleic acid, a high omega-6 to omega-3 ratio and industrial solvent extraction. Nutrition reviews report that linoleic acid does not reliably raise inflammatory markers and that swapping saturated for unsaturated fat is linked to better cardiovascular markers. No studies have tested seed oil avoidance for skin or facial appearance.
quick.how: Followers read labels, cook at home and swap oils for butter, tallow, ghee or olive oil, and often pair it with carnivore or primal eating or other clean-eating habits. Restaurants and packaged foods are the hard part, since seed oils are widely used. Users report judging results over several weeks.
quick.risks: Avoiding seed oils is not itself documented as harmful, but reviews note that shifting toward saturated fat could raise LDL cholesterol. Health bodies generally continue to recommend unsaturated oils over saturated fats. Strict avoidance can make eating out difficult.

angle.text: Followers cut canola, soybean, sunflower and similar oils expecting lower inflammation, clearer skin and less puffiness. It is bundled with other clean-eating habits in looksmaxxing forums; nutrition reviews generally report that these oils do not reliably raise inflammation markers.

fasting-for-face-fat.summary: Intermittent fasting used to lower body fat and slim the face; trials show weight loss similar to ordinary calorie reduction.

quick.overview:
Fasting for face fat means using intermittent fasting, such as a daily eating window, alternate days or 5:2, to lose body fat and reveal a leaner, more defined face. It sits alongside cutting and 'leanmaxxing' and hollow-cheek aesthetics.

Fasting lowers calorie intake and lengthens overnight fasting intervals. A 2025 BMJ network meta-analysis of 99 randomized trials in 6,582 adults found weight loss roughly comparable to ordinary calorie restriction. No study has measured facial fat after fasting, and where fat comes off varies by person and genetics.
quick.how: Most people pick a time-restricted window or a few lower-calorie days a week and pair it with their usual cutting routine. Weight changes show up over weeks to months, and faces slim as overall body fat falls. Some report that people with low body fat still keep fuller faces.
quick.risks: Hunger, irritability, dizziness and headache are reported. Fasting is not recommended for pregnant or breastfeeding women, children, underweight people or those prone to eating disorders. Forum members raise concerns about testosterone, thyroid and muscle, and a 2025 Cell study reported that intermittent fasting suppressed hair follicle regeneration.

angle.text: Users adopt intermittent fasting to lower overall calorie intake and body fat, which slims the face and sharpens cheek and jaw definition. Trials show weight loss comparable to ordinary calorie reduction; how much of it comes off the face varies by person.

extreme-dieting-low-body-fat.summary: Cutting to very low body fat for a defined jaw, cheekbones and visible muscle, the approach called leanmaxxing.

quick.overview:
Leanmaxxing means sustained calorie deficits to reach very low body fat, with forum targets of about 10 to 15%, aiming for a sharper jaw, visible cheekbones and defined muscle. Members disagree on the ideal level, and some report their face stayed full even when lean.

A sustained energy deficit reduces fat stores across the body, and where fat leaves first varies by person. Sports-science reviews describe how bodybuilders and weight-class athletes diet for contests, including higher protein intake during deficits, and typically hold extreme leanness only briefly.
quick.how: People run a long calorie deficit, often with high protein and resistance training to hold muscle, and track weight and photos over months. Competitors in physique sports hold peak leanness only for the contest period.
quick.risks: The IOC and the RED-S literature document hormonal, bone, mood and performance problems from prolonged low energy availability in men and women, including lower androgen levels, bone density and strength in men. Disordered eating is a recognised concern in weight-sensitive sports.

angle.text: Leanmaxxing means a prolonged calorie deficit to reach roughly 10 to 15% body fat, which reveals the jaw, cheekbones and muscle definition. Facial fat distribution is partly genetic, so how much the face changes varies, and sports medicine documents the practice in competition prep.

tapeworm-diet.summary: An old fad-diet story in which a swallowed tapeworm absorbs food to cause weight loss; medical sources describe tapeworm infection as a disease.

quick.overview:
The tapeworm diet is a long-running diet legend: a person deliberately swallows a tapeworm so it absorbs part of the food they eat, aiming for weight loss and a leaner look, then takes an anti-parasitic drug at the goal weight. Wikipedia lists it among 19th-century diet hoaxes.

The idea is that the worm competes with the host for nutrients. Medical sources describe taeniasis as often causing mild or no symptoms, with weight loss only an occasional sign of infection. No clinical studies have tested it as a weight-loss method.
quick.how: It circulates mainly as a story about extreme dieting rather than a routine with a defined method. In the legend, the worm is carried until the target weight is reached and then removed with medication.
quick.risks: Wikipedia notes gastric obstruction risk in the diet story. Cysticercosis from Taenia solium eggs can reach the brain, eyes and muscles and be serious or fatal, and the fish tapeworm can cause pernicious anemia by interfering with B12 absorption. Medical sources treat tapeworm infection as a disease requiring treatment.

angle.text: The story is that a swallowed tapeworm absorbs part of the food eaten, so fewer calories are taken in and the body and face slim down. It appears in accounts of 19th-century diet hoaxes, and medical sources describe the infection as a disease with serious risks.

cold-showers.summary: Cold-water showers taken for mood, discipline and claimed skin, hair and testosterone benefits; meta-analyses report mood and stress signals.

quick.overview:
Cold showers are taken for claimed benefits to skin, hair, testosterone, mood and discipline. Users post that skin and hair look better; others say cold showers make eye bags or features look harsher.

Cold exposure triggers the cold shock response, vasoconstriction and a surge in the sympathetic nervous system, and repeated cold showers reduce the initial response to later cold immersion. Meta-analyses of cold-water exposure report pooled signals toward better mood, perceived stress and wellbeing, with wide confidence intervals. No study has tested cold showers for skin appearance or testosterone.
quick.how: People end a normal shower with a cold blast or take the whole shower cold, often as a morning routine, building up duration over days to weeks. It overlaps with ice baths, cold plunges and the Wim Hof Method.
quick.risks: Cold-water immersion can cause gasping, heart rate and blood pressure surges, and arrhythmias in some people. The American Heart Association and British Heart Foundation advise consulting a physician before cold therapy. Combining breath-holding or hyperventilation with water has been linked to blackout and drowning reports.

angle.text: Users take cold showers expecting tighter-looking, healthier skin, better hair and a mood and discipline lift, through a circulation and stress-response jolt. Meta-analyses report mood and stress effects; skin, hair and hormone claims come from user reports.

cold-plunge-face-ice-dunk.summary: Dunking the face, or whole body, in ice water to reduce morning puffiness and tighten the look of the skin.

quick.overview:
A face ice dunk means submerging the face in a bowl of ice water for a short time to cut morning puffiness and tighten the look of the skin. A cold plunge is the whole-body version in a tub of cold water, more often tied to recovery. Both are low-cost routines popular in appearance communities.

Cold constricts blood vessels near the skin and lowers local metabolic activity, which proponents say reduces fluid pooling and swelling. No published human study has tested face dunking for depuffing. Related research covers whole-body cold-water immersion for exercise recovery and cold therapy for swelling after injury, both described as mixed.
quick.how: People fill a bowl with water and ice and hold the face in for short intervals, usually in the morning, repeating several times. Others use whole-body plunges or ice baths in a tub. Effects on puffiness are judged by how the face looks that morning.
quick.risks: Cold shock response, cardiac stress, hypothermia and cold burns are documented risks of cold exposure, mostly with whole-body immersion; one British death during cold-water therapy was reported in 2022. Cold allergy and circulation disorders are listed contraindications. Face-specific risks are not well studied.

angle.text: Looksmaxxing users dunk the face in ice water to constrict blood vessels and reduce morning puffiness, giving a tighter, more defined look. Whole-body plunges are tied more to recovery. No published trials have tested the facial routine.

sungazing.summary: Looking directly at the sun near sunrise or sunset for claimed eyesight, mood, skin and iris-colour effects; ophthalmology literature documents retinal burns from it.

quick.overview:
Sungazing is looking directly at the sun, usually near dawn or dusk, as a spiritual or health practice. In looksmaxxing forums users discuss it for eyesight, mood, skin and lighter eye colour. William Horatio Bates promoted it in the early 20th century as 'sunning' in his eye exercises for myopia.

Proponents say sunlight entering the eyes affects hormones, circadian rhythm and mood, and some believe it changes iris pigment. No published trial has tested vision or appearance benefits. Ophthalmology literature describes a different outcome: high-energy visible and ultraviolet light can damage retinal cells, and the retina has no pain receptors, so injury can go unnoticed.
quick.how: Practitioners look toward the sun for short periods near sunrise or sunset, as a daily ritual. Some users post about their own experiences, including floaters.
quick.risks: Solar retinopathy typically causes central blind spots, distorted vision and light sensitivity. Many cases recover over weeks to six months, but some produce lasting foveal defects. Reviews and case reports also link repeated bright-light exposure to concerns about macular degeneration.

angle.text: Some users look at the sun hoping for lighter iris colour, sharper vision and a mood lift through light exposure to the eyes. The practice dates to early 20th-century eye exercises, and ophthalmology literature documents retinal burns from direct sun viewing.

urine-therapy.summary: Drinking or applying urine for skin and rejuvenation, a tradition with roots in yoga and naturopathy; medical sources report no demonstrated benefit.

quick.overview:
Urine therapy, also called urotherapy or shivambu, means drinking one's own urine or applying it to the skin or gums for health or cosmetic purposes, with the aim of clearer, younger-looking skin. It has roots in several cultures, including medieval hatha yoga, and was popularised in modern times by the British naturopath John W. Armstrong.

Proponents attribute effects to substances in urine, such as urea or claimed stem cells. Urine is over 95 percent water, and commercial urea creams use synthetic urea at far higher concentrations than urine provides. A reference source states there is no scientific evidence of therapeutic benefit from untreated urine.
quick.how: Followers drink their own urine, sometimes aged, or massage it into skin or gums, typically as a daily morning routine. Some apply it as a facial toner.
quick.risks: Medical sources report no demonstrated benefit and note microbial contamination concerns. The American Cancer Society states that evidence does not support urine or urea helping cancer patients. One looksmax.org user posted a report of a negative experience drinking aged urine, describing a burning throat and nausea.

angle.text: Followers drink or apply urine, sometimes aged, hoping for skin renewal and a younger, clearer look. The practice has roots in yoga traditions, and medical sources report no demonstrated therapeutic benefit from untreated urine.

sunbathing-tanmaxxing.summary: Darkening the skin with sun, lamps or sunless products for a warmer, healthier-looking complexion; the change is visible straight away.

quick.overview:
Tanmaxxing means darkening the skin with sunbathing, tanning lotions, lamps or sunless products for a warmer, healthier-looking complexion. Tanned skin has been fashionable in the West since the 1920s, and looksmaxxing guides treat colour as part of skin and overall appearance.

UV radiation prompts melanocytes to make melanin. UVA darkens existing pigment, while UVB causes DNA damage that triggers new melanin and a tan that appears a few days later. Sunless self-tanners using dihydroxyacetone react with proteins in the outer skin layer to produce a brown colour without UV.
quick.how: People get gradual sun exposure, use tanning lotions or oils, visit tanning beds, or apply sunless self-tanner, which gives colour within hours. UV tans build over days to weeks. Sun exposure also supports vitamin D production.
quick.risks: Excess UV is associated with sunburn, DNA mutations, skin cancer, accelerated skin ageing and immune suppression. A 2010 study linked frequent tanning bed use to about triple the melanoma risk. The WHO, American Cancer Society and US Surgeon General warn against excessive sun and indoor tanning. Fair skin burns more easily.

angle.text: Tanmaxxing darkens the skin with sun, lamps, lotions or sunless products for a warmer, healthier-looking complexion, and the colour change shows right away. Tanning is the skin's pigment response to UV; sunless products based on dihydroxyacetone give colour without UV.

sleepmaxxing.summary: Optimising sleep with darkness, routines, light control and sometimes supplements, aiming for brighter skin, fewer eye bags and better recovery.

quick.overview:
Sleepmaxxing means optimising sleep, typically with a dark, cool, quiet bedroom, a fixed schedule, limited evening light and food, and sometimes blue-light-blocking glasses or supplements. People aim for brighter skin, fewer dark circles, less puffiness and better recovery and energy.

Proponents say regular timing and darkness steady the circadian rhythm, which they link to melatonin production, sleep quality and next-day appearance. Most of it overlaps with sleep hygiene, developed in the late 1970s; a 2014 review described the evidence that it improves sleep as weak and inconclusive, though some individual items have stronger support.
quick.how: Routines include blackout curtains, cooling bedding, sunrise lamps, a set bedtime and wake time, blue-light avoidance and cutting alcohol or late meals. Some add supplements, and forum threads also discuss research peptides. People check results over a few weeks.
quick.risks: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine concluded in 2021 that sleep hygiene should not be used alone as therapy for chronic insomnia, warning it could delay effective treatment. A forum guide notes that sleep medication can lose effect with daily use and that melatonin may disturb the circadian rhythm if taken daily. Peptides discussed in threads are unapproved.

angle.text: Better sleep helps recovery, hormones and skin, which users expect to show up as brighter skin, fewer eye bags and less puffiness. Routines combine darkness, fixed timing and light control; sleep hygiene research focuses on sleep quality rather than appearance.

smellmaxxing.summary: Managing body scent with hygiene, deodorant, diet and fragrance so you smell good and come across as more attractive.

quick.overview:
Smellmaxxing means improving how you smell, through hygiene, deodorant, diet or fragrance, on the idea that scent adds to attractiveness. A forum thread has asked whether good smell can compensate for looks.

Most body odour comes from bacteria acting on secretions of apocrine glands, which become active at puberty and are concentrated in the armpits. Genetics, notably the ABCC11 gene, and diet also affect odour. Studies report that women tend to prefer the scent of men whose immune genes differ from their own, and that fruit and vegetable intake was linked to sweat described as more pleasant.
quick.how: People shower regularly, use deodorant or antiperspirant, wash clothes and bedding, care for oral hygiene and choose a fragrance. Deodorants reduce odour, while antiperspirants block sweat pores temporarily. Results are immediate on application.
quick.risks: No notable harms are documented for ordinary hygiene or fragrance use in the sources reviewed. Studies on scent and attraction are small and do not establish how much scent affects perceived attractiveness.

angle.text: Smellmaxxing manages body scent with hygiene, deodorant and fragrance so you smell fresher and come across as more attractive up close. The effect is immediate; body-odour science describes bacteria, genes and diet as the main contributors.

gymmaxxing.summary: Lifting and leaning out for looks, building broader shoulders and a leaner physique through resistance training and diet.

quick.overview:
Gymmaxxing means resistance training and eating to build muscle and reduce body fat in order to look better, usually with an emphasis on leanness and shoulder width. It is one of the most commonly recommended softmaxxes in looksmaxxing communities, and users post before-and-after transformation photos.

Resistance training places mechanical tension on muscle, which activates growth signalling, and results depend on training volume, progressive overload, nutrition and individual genetics. The exercise science behind muscle gain is well established. How much it raises rated attractiveness or dating outcomes has been debated on forums and not tested directly.
quick.how: People follow progressive lifting programmes several days a week, eat enough protein, and alternate muscle-gain and fat-loss phases. Visible changes in muscle and leanness typically build over months to years. Forum guides cover training theory and form.
quick.risks: Training carries ordinary injury risks, and forum guides warn about ego lifting and poor form. Forum threads also discuss anabolic steroids alongside gymmaxxing, a separate topic with documented medical risks.

angle.text: Progressive resistance training builds muscle and, with diet, lowers body fat, giving broader shoulders, a leaner waist and a more athletic frame. Muscle-building physiology is well described; how much it shifts attractiveness is debated on forums.

alcohol-sugar-dairy-face-avoidance.summary: Dropping alcohol, added sugar and dairy for a leaner, less puffy, clearer-looking face.

quick.overview:
This diet-side softmaxx means cutting alcohol, added sugar and dairy to get a leaner, less puffy and clearer face, often alongside fat loss.

Proposed routes are lower body fat, less fluid retention, better sleep and fewer acne flares. Wikipedia reports that trials and observational work link high-glycemic-load diets with acne, that evidence tying milk to acne is weak and observational, and that alcohol is a diuretic that disrupts sleep and triggers flushing in rosacea. No study has tested removing all three for facial appearance.
quick.how: People remove drinks, sweets, sugary foods and dairy products, often as part of a cutting phase or a cleaner-eating reset, and watch their face and skin over a few weeks.
quick.risks: Removing foods is generally low risk, but very restrictive diets can cause nutritional shortfalls, and severe dieting practices carry health risks.

angle.text: Cutting alcohol, added sugar and dairy is meant to lower water retention, calm acne and support fat loss and sleep, giving a leaner, clearer, less puffy face. Acne and hydration research exists on the individual foods; facial leanness itself has not been measured.

softmaxxing.summary: The non-invasive end of looksmaxxing, covering skincare, haircuts, grooming, clothing, posture, sleep and fitness, all low-risk and reversible.

quick.overview:
Softmaxxing is the looksmaxxing name for reversible, low-risk improvements such as skincare, haircuts, grooming, clothing, posture, sleep and exercise. It is set against hardmaxxing, which covers surgery and drugs, and forum users commonly advise doing softmaxxes first.

The payoff is cleaner skin, tidier grooming, better body composition and a sharper overall presentation, much of it visible quickly. A looksmax.org guide defines it as non-invasive, reversible, low-risk improvements that raise attractiveness without surgery or medical intervention. The components have their own research, mostly from dermatology and general health guidance, and no trial has tested softmaxxing as a package.
quick.how: Typical basics include twice-daily cleansing, daily sunscreen, oral hygiene, a flattering haircut, well-fitted clothes, good posture, lifting and weight management. Some people add less conventional practices such as mewing and NoFap, which Grokipedia says have little scientific support.
quick.risks: Most components are low risk. Researchers have noted that online skincare content mixes commercial claims with advice and can encourage irritating self-experimentation, and critics link looksmaxxing culture generally to body-image distress.

angle.text: Softmaxxing covers skincare, haircuts, grooming, clothing, posture and weight management, giving cleaner, healthier-looking presentation with no surgery. Forum guides describe it as low-risk and reversible, and many of the habits show visible results quickly.

body-dysmorphia-mirror-checking.summary: Compulsive mirror checking and appearance fixation: the mental-health side of looksmaxxing, a recognised condition (BDD) that CBT and SSRIs treat.

quick.overview:
Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) is a psychiatric condition in which a person spends hours on perceived flaws that others barely notice, with mirror checking, comparing, reassurance seeking and camouflage as typical behaviours. Some people avoid mirrors instead. Knowing it helps people on appearance-focused forums tell the difference between improving how they look and being stuck in distress about it.

Looksmaxxing communities involve heavy self-scrutiny, and critics cited by Wikipedia link the culture to body dysmorphia. Clinical models treat checking and similar behaviours as maintaining the appearance concern. No controlled study establishes how often BDD occurs in these communities.
quick.how: Clinical treatment centres on cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and ritual prevention, and on serotonin reuptake inhibitors, delivered through mental health professionals. Cutting back on checking, comparing and reassurance seeking is part of that work.
quick.risks: Reviews report significant impairment, frequent comorbid depression and anxiety, and relatively common suicidal ideation. According to Wikipedia, cosmetic treatment typically does not relieve the distress, and BDD is often underdiagnosed. Anyone in crisis can reach local emergency or crisis lines.

angle.text: Body dysmorphic disorder and mirror checking are the mental-health side of appearance focus, where fixation on minor perceived flaws distorts self-view. It is a recognised psychiatric condition, and clinicians treat it with CBT and SSRIs, which can improve confidence and presence.

subliminals-for-appearance.summary: Audio tracks with hidden affirmations that listeners hope will change height, eye colour, jaw growth or hair loss through the subconscious.

quick.overview:
Appearance subliminals are audio recordings that supposedly carry hidden affirmations below conscious hearing, with listeners hoping for features like extra height, a different eye colour, jaw growth or less hair loss. They circulate on looksmaxxing forums and on subreddits dedicated to the practice.

Believers say the subconscious mind can be influenced by sub-audible affirmations. Laboratory research on subliminal stimuli has found effects on brain activity and on actions a person already intends to take, with limited, context-dependent results. No study has tested these recordings for physical change, and one self-concept trial found effects resembling placebo apart from a self-concept change.
quick.how: Listeners play tracks, often layered under music, for long stretches each day or while sleeping, over weeks to months. Forum members are split between those reporting results and those who attribute them to expectation.
quick.risks: Direct physical risk is low. Wikipedia notes subliminal advertising is prohibited in several countries.

angle.text: Listeners play subliminal audio hoping to grow taller, change eye colour, improve jaw growth or reduce hair loss through the subconscious. No study has tested physical change from these recordings, and forum members are split, with some crediting expectation.

colloidal-silver.summary: Ingested silver suspension sold as an immune supplement that also turns up in eye colour discussions; chronic use can cause permanent blue-grey skin (argyria).

quick.overview:
Colloidal silver is a suspension of very small silver particles that alternative-health sources promote as a supplement for immunity and general health, and it appears in appearance forums in eye colour discussions. It has a long history as an antimicrobial and was registered as a biocide in the US in 1954.

Silver particles have antimicrobial properties in laboratory and wound-dressing contexts and are used in medical devices and textiles. Wikipedia states no medical evidence supports ingesting it for the claimed uses, and silver is not an essential mineral. Reviews say ingested nanosilver is not inert and distributes to tissues such as the liver. Its best-documented appearance effect is argyria, a blue-grey skin colour.
quick.how: People take it as a liquid supplement by mouth, as sold in alternative-health circles, and use silver in dressings and sinus rinses. Marketing has claimed uses against conditions including cancer, diabetes and arthritis.
quick.risks: Chronic ingestion or inhalation of silver can cause argyria, which Wikipedia says does not resolve after exposure stops. Reviews report liver and lung effects of inhaled nanosilver in rats, and the US EPA classifies antimicrobial silver nanoparticles as pesticides.

angle.text: Colloidal silver is taken as an immune and general-health supplement and appears in eye colour discussions. Wikipedia states no medical evidence supports the health claims, and chronic use can cause permanent blue-grey skin discolouration (argyria).

eye-color-change-drops.summary: Drops, and the wider set of eye colour procedures, that people hope will lighten brown eyes toward blue, green or hazel.

quick.overview:
People discuss drops, including latanoprost-type and homemade ones, to lighten brown eyes toward blue, green or hazel. Iris colour depends largely on the melanin in the iris stroma. No peer-reviewed study has tested a cosmetic drop for lightening. Latanoprost, a glaucoma medicine, is labelled to increase brown iris pigment, so its documented effect runs toward darker eyes.

Forum conversation mostly moves to procedures. Keratopigmentation places pigment in the cornea, laser depigmentation uses a Nd:YAG laser to remove stromal melanin, and implants cover the iris with a coloured artificial disc. Reviews describe keratopigmentation as the best studied option, laser as having limited long-term data and implants as the weakest on safety.
quick.how: Forum users compare drops, corneal tattooing, laser depigmentation and iris implants, with the procedures done by eye surgeons or clinics abroad. Results from procedures are visible once healed, and forum posters themselves raise contamination concerns about homemade drops.
quick.risks: Reviews report that cosmetic iris implants are not approved by major regulators and have been linked to glaucoma, uveitis, corneal damage and vision loss. Laser depigmentation has limited long-term safety data, and keratopigmentation still lacks long-term cosmetic evidence. Unregulated drops placed in the eye carry general risks of contamination and infection.

angle.text: Users discuss drops, including latanoprost-type and homemade ones, to lighten brown eyes toward blue, green or hazel, alongside keratopigmentation, laser depigmentation and implants. No peer-reviewed study has tested a cosmetic drop for this; latanoprost is documented to darken irises, and surgical routes carry documented eye risks.
